query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for jet-turbine applications, what single intervention could improve high-temperature mechanical capability while limiting density and preserving room-temperature performance? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its mechanism, the expected improvement relative to a relevant baseline, the temperature and loading conditions under which it should hold, supporting evidence from prior studies, and a decisive experiment with a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 5 wt% tungsten to a refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature mechanical capability by 20% at 1000°C under tensile loading, relative to the baseline alloy without tungsten addition, while maintaining a density below 8.5 g/cm³ and preserving room-temperature yield strength within 10% of the baseline value.
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloy in the as-cast state
generation.intervention: Addition of 5 wt% tungsten to the alloy composition
generation.structural_mediator: Solid-solution strengthening and precipitation of tungsten-rich phases
generation.mechanism: The added tungsten will form a solid solution with the other alloying elements, increasing the lattice distortion and thus the strength of the alloy at high temperatures. Additionally, the precipitation of tungsten-rich phases will provide further strengthening through dispersion hardening.
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% improvement in high-temperature mechanical capability, as measured by the yield strength at 1000°C
generation.baseline: Refractory high-entropy alloy without tungsten addition, with a yield strength of 500 MPa at 1000°C
generation.boundary: Density below 8.5 g/cm³ and room-temperature yield strength within 10% of the baseline value (450-550 MPa)
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in high-temperature mechanical capability may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions. The precipitation of tungsten-rich phases may also affect the alloy's ductility and toughness.

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of the tungsten-containing alloy and the baseline alloy at 1000°C
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength of the tungsten-containing alloy at 1000°C is not at least 15% higher than that of the baseline alloy, or if the density exceeds 8.5 g/cm³, or if the room-temperature yield strength deviates by more than 15% from the baseline value, the hypothesis is falsified.

goal.constraint: limiting density and preserving room-temperature performance

prior_attempts: prior studies on refractory high-entropy alloys

families.principle: alloying elements affecting phase stability and strength
microstructural features influencing strength and toughness
processing conditions influencing grain size and distribution
thermal treatment affecting precipitate formation and dislocation density
surface coatings or treatments affecting oxidation resistance and fatigue life
